canonicalExplanation.summary: A **formatter** (Prettier, Black, gofmt) rewrites **layout**: indentation, quotes, line breaks. It never changes behaviour and settles style arguments. A **linter** (ESLint, Ruff, Pylint) **reports patterns**: unused variables, `==` instead of `===`, unsafe `eval`, possible bugs. They're different tools. Pin both as **dev dependencies with committed config**, so everyone and CI run the **same version**. Keep formatting changes in **their own commit**, separate from logic fixes. And remember: passing both doesn't mean the code is correct or secure. They catch patterns, not wrong logic.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner fixes a one-line bug, but their editor's formatter (a different version from CI's) reformats the whole file. The PR shows 300 changed lines, the reviewer can't find the fix, and CI fails the format check anyway. Formatting changes are separated from a logic fix so reviewers can see behavior clearly while CI enforces the same formatter version. In this lesson you'll configure and apply formatter and linter checks to changed files.

sections.heading: The distinction: formatter rewrites, linter reports
sections.body:
```bash
npm install --save-dev prettier@3.3.3 eslint@9.9.0   # pinned in the lockfile.
# Config committed: .prettierrc, eslint.config.js.

npx prettier --check src/          # CI: fail if anything isn't formatted.
npx prettier --write src/cart.js   # locally: rewrite layout.
npx eslint src/cart.js             # report problems.
#   12:7  error  'total' is assigned a value but never used  no-unused-vars.
#   20:9  error  Expected '===' and instead saw '=='         eqeqeq.
```

| | Formatter | Linter |
|---|---|---|
| changes files? | yes (layout only). | only with --fix, for some rules. |
| finds possible bugs? | no. | some patterns. |
| settles style debates? | yes. | partly. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "How do you add a formatter to an old project without drowning every PR?", "answer": "Format everything in one dedicated commit (\"Apply Prettier to codebase\") with no logic changes, and list its hash in .git-blame-ignore-revs so blame skips it."}
```

sections.heading: Keep diffs readable

examples.title: Separating formatting from the fix
examples.situation: Formatting changes are separated from a logic fix so reviewers can see behavior clearly while CI enforces the same formatter version.
walkthrough: **Same formatter version:** prettier@3.3.3 is pinned, so the editor and CI agree.
**Formatting changes are separated:** commit one runs prettier --write only; commit two changes `==` to `===` in the total check.
**Reviewers can see behavior clearly:** the fix commit's diff is one line, and CI will run prettier --check with the same version.
examples.result: The review takes a minute, and CI passes.

examples.title: The linter warning that was a bug
examples.situation: ESLint reports `no-unused-vars` for `discount` in checkout.js. The learner is tempted to disable the rule.
walkthrough: Reading the line shows discount was calculated but never subtracted.
The warning pointed at a real logic bug.
Fix the code; don't silence the rule.
examples.result: Customers get their discount, thanks to one lint warning.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Formatter and linter are synonyms, and code that passes both cannot contain bugs or security flaws.
misconceptions.correction: A formatter changes layout; a linter reports configured patterns. Neither understands your requirements, so wrong logic and many security flaws pass both.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what can pass both tools?

analogy.example: A formatter is like **a typesetter** laying out a book neatly. A linter is **a copy editor** flagging suspicious sentences. Neither checks whether the story's facts are true; that's tests and review.
limitations: Typesetters never change words; formatters never change behaviour.
Copy editors can be configured; so can linters.

nearTransfer.prompt: Add a pinned formatter and linter to a small project with committed config. Run both on one file, fix the lint errors, and explain each one.

farTransfer.prompt: Introduce a formatter to an existing project: one formatting-only commit listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs, a CI check with the pinned version, and a follow-up logic fix whose diff is small. Show git blame skipping the formatting commit.

remediation.explanation: Ask: **is this change layout or behaviour?** Layout goes in a formatting commit; behaviour gets its own. And treat lint warnings as **possible bugs to read**, not noise to silence.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The linter warning that was a bug".

recap.summary: To configure and apply formatter and linter checks, pin both tools with committed configuration so every machine and CI use the same versions, run them on changed files, keep formatting in separate commits from logic, and remember neither proves the code is correct or secure.
